task.description: Observed during the GB-127 namespace reservation: crates.io returns 429 with the deadline only in the message body ('You have published too many new crates in a short period of time. Please try again after Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:30:25 GMT') and no Retry-After header. parse_cooldown matched neither 'retry after <n>' nor 'try again in <n>', so it fell back to the 30s default and the 3-attempt budget was exhausted before the real ~2 minute cooldown elapsed. Add a 'try again after <RFC2822>' form plus a generic HTTP-date scan.
task.title: parse_cooldown misses crates.io's 'try again after <RFC2822 date>' body form

receipt.summary: Merged to outfeed main (9f84ff1): parse_cooldown resolves an explicit Retry-After token first, then prose deadlines as RFC 2822 dates before any bare integer (a day-of-month was previously read as 28 seconds), then scans the whole output as a last resort. Reproduced with the verbatim crates.io 429 body observed during the GB-127 reservation; gates: clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, nextest --workspace 67/67, fmt OK, docs 9/9.
